Write 25 register values from $505F through $5077 to the SID beginning at $D400. The loop descends from the master-volume register to voice 1 frequency.
Read $D012 until its low byte changes. Resample if the subtraction in the comparison is negative.
Load driver and road-phase state to set the self-modifying operands used in the raster drawing path.

Acknowledge the VIC IRQ, wait for the raster offset in $10 plus six lines and change character memory and background colour for the road band. Hand the vector to $36B8 and enter its common palette writer with the current driver's two background colours.

Acknowledge the VIC IRQ. While $15 is nonnegative, XOR background colours $D022 and $D023 with $0A and $03, and schedule the next change using $60A0 indexed by the band counter. A negative counter goes to the later band handler at $375C.

Save the interrupted registers and acknowledge the VIC raster flag at the end of the road band. Reached through the vector installed at $3707/$370C.

Copy the current view selector to $17, then toggle $16 at the raster line in $18. Set the vector back to $3ECD, blank five sprite slots with image $30 and switch the display to the dashboard character bank.
Immediate operand of the X load at $3777. That X selects the VIC screen and character base written at $378C.

Set dashboard background colour, clear bit 7 in the next driver's display state and program the next interrupt line. Load timing operands from the road-band tables for racing, or call the pit display paths for a driver in the pits.

Save the outer interrupt’s registers in the immediate operands of its return path and allow the raster IRQs to interrupt the game update. Update voice 3 and sample both joysticks for view 0. Then update the elapsed time and dispatch the selected driver to racing, pit activity or the end-of-tick work.
Read both active-low CIA1 joystick ports in the order selected by $7C at the starting grid. Store the two readings at $03D2 and $03D3 before the per-driver update.

Read a forced control byte, an AI input or the matching stored joystick value according to driver state and player count. Shift the active-low bits through carry to apply acceleration, braking and lateral movement to the selected driver.
Shift the accelerate bit into carry and, if it is low, add $12 to the two-byte speed at $45,X and $48,X. Cap forward acceleration at $29FF, then process the brake bit and write the final speed.
Read left and right from successive shifts of $25. Change signed lateral velocity at $6E,X and $70,X within its bounds before the turbo path.
If the shifted fire bit is low, set the turbo indicator and add $09 to the current speed, retaining the $29FF cap.
Accept the pit-entry transition when the road selector is in $15–$1E and the preceding horizontal boundary test succeeds. Clear speed and lateral-motion state and store pit state 1 at $50,X.
Inspect the four tyre-state entries for the selected driver. Cap wear at 7 and on the first transition set $76,X and start the voice-3 noise effect.
Decay signed lateral velocity towards zero in $0080 steps, or clear it if there is no forward motion or state in $76,X.
Derive a road animation increment from current speed divided by eight. Add it to the fine and coarse phase; on a coarse wrap or raster-table change, toggle the two road palette values.

Select the per-driver SID register offset at $5078 and set the sawtooth pitch from the speed bytes. The high-byte calculation folds speed at two thresholds before combining it with the low byte. Disable that voice’s gate when the driver status byte is negative.
